justification: Terrain diagram never rendered because the DEM fetch failed on timeout. LIVE-probed both endpoints: GA WCS (the primary) returns a ServiceException/400 — its 2.0.1 subset used axis labels Long/Lat but the coverage's real labels are y/x (EPSG:4283), giving InvalidAxisLabel; corrected to y/x (GA still rejects on another param, but this removes the definitively-wrong label and is no regression since GA already failed). The working path is NSW SIX Maps exportImage, which returns a valid GeoTIFF but takes ~26s — longer than the old _TIMEOUT=20, so it was always killed before responding. Raised _TIMEOUT to 40s (SIX Maps's typical latency, still inside the brief's 55s terrain budget) and capped GA at 12s so the broken primary cannot starve the working fallback. SIX Maps latency is variable (sometimes >40s) so terrain remains best-effort; the durable fix is Tier-3 precompute (terrain barely changes per lot).

pre_impl.existing_data: fetch_dem_region tries GA WCS 1.0.0, GA WCS 2.0.1, then SIX Maps exportImage, each with a single shared _TIMEOUT=20. The brief calls run_terrain_analysis(include_flood=False) so exactly one fetch_dem_region(500m) runs per brief.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed the DEM endpoints were simply down; in fact SIX Maps works but is slow (26s) and GA's WCS 2.0.1 axis labels were wrong (Long/Lat vs y/x).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new mechanism — adjusted the existing timeout constant, added a GA-specific cap, and corrected the WCS 2.0.1 axis labels.
pre_impl.external_source_error: GA WCS returns an OGC ServiceException / ArcGIS 400; the code already treats a non-TIFF GA response as failure and falls through to SIX Maps. A SIX Maps timeout is caught and surfaces as a NOT_AVAILABLE terrain section (honest 'unavailable' card), never a fabricated diagram.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: terrain always showed 'unavailable' (no diagram) because the 20s timeout killed the 26s SIX Maps fetch. After: the diagram renders whenever SIX Maps responds within 40s (the common case); a slow/failed fetch still shows an honest unavailable card.

functions.name: _fetch_ga_wcs
functions.input: lat, lng, buffer_m in metres, and a timeout in seconds
functions.output: a GeoTIFF BytesIO from GA WCS, or None on failure; its timeout is now capped at 12s and its 2.0.1 subset uses the correct y/x axis labels
functions.if_none: returns None so fetch_dem_region falls through to SIX Maps

functions.name: fetch_dem_region
functions.output: a DEM GeoTIFF BytesIO from GA or SIX Maps
functions.if_none: raises RuntimeError if both sources fail; the caller maps this to a NOT_AVAILABLE terrain section

values: N/A - elevation raster bytes, not regulatory values.
queries: N/A - external WCS/ImageServer HTTP only; no DB.

break_it.scenario: SIX Maps takes longer than 40s for a large/slow region
break_it.what_happens: the DEM fetch times out and terrain shows an honest unavailable card
break_it.repro: request a 5000m buffer or hit the service under load
break_it.how: the timeout is caught; terrain surfaces NOT_AVAILABLE with a reason rather than a fabricated or partial diagram. The brief uses the small 500m buffer, the common-case path

break_it.scenario: GA WCS starts hanging instead of fast-failing
break_it.what_happens: a slow primary could eat the terrain budget before SIX Maps is tried
break_it.how: GA is capped at 12s per attempt (min(timeout, _GA_TIMEOUT_CAP)), bounding the wasted time to ~24s and leaving SIX Maps room inside the 55s budget

break_it.scenario: GA WCS begins returning TIFFs again with the corrected y/x labels
break_it.what_happens: GA LiDAR would be served instead of SIX Maps
break_it.repro: GA fixes its remaining param rejection
break_it.how: that is the preferred higher-quality source; _is_tiff validates the response before returning, so a non-TIFF GA reply still falls through to SIX Maps

post_merge.secrets: None - both DEM endpoints are keyless public services.
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the standalone terrain satellite tool uses the same fetch_dem_region and benefits identically.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run a brief with satellite on for an inner-Sydney address: the Terrain Analysis card now renders the shaded-relief diagram when SIX Maps responds within 40s; otherwise it shows an honest 'unavailable' state.
